raw_case_text: A 58-year-old male had a history of end-stage renal failure with 3 kidney transplantations (1979, 1981 and 2008). He had previous chronic hepatitis B, legionellosis, chronic Q fever and cytomegalovirus infection. The last renal transplantation was associated with acute rejection requiring a combination of anti-thymoglobulin, plasma exchanges, rituximab, mycophenolate mofetil 1g/d, tacrolimus 4.5mg/d and prednisone 10 mg/d. In 2004 Leishmania PCR in blood was positive (Fig 1B). L-AmB treatment initially induced clinical cure. Relapse occurred in August 2009 when plasma exchanges and corticosteroids boluses were administered for the graft rejection. Fever, anemia (Hb = 9.1g/dL) and leukopenia (leukocytes = 1600/mm3) were observed, along with 431 Leishmania per ml of blood (assessed by quantitative PCR). L-AmB (induction total dose, 40 mg/Kg) provided improvement and reduced parasitemia to 6.9 Leishmania/ml. A second recurrence with fever and a rise in parasitemia to 29.6 Leishmania/ml occurred in January 2010 during monthly maintenance administration of 3 mg/kg of L-AmB. High-dose L-AmB was reintroduced followed by miltefosine for 4 months. Parasitemia decreased but remained positive (0.4 Leishmania/ml) and number of CD4 lymphocytes increased from 87 to 147/mm3. A third recurrence was reported in July 2010 with fever, 29.8 Leishmania/ml and positive Leishmania culture from venous blood. L-AmB was reintroduced, followed by maintenance infusions for 4 months, 3 mg/Kg every 3 weeks plus downgrading of immunosuppressive therapies. As symptoms persisted, infusions were performed once-weekly and then twice-weekly. Parasitemia decreased from 88 to 0.6 Leishmania/ml but a fourth recurrence occurred in April-June 2011 with fever, leukopenia (leukocytes = 1200/mm3, CD4 lymphocytes = 186/mm3), anemia (Hb = 9.1g/dL) and parasitemia at 40 Leishmania/ml. Patient refused to increase the L-AmB dose, it continued at 3 mg/Kg twice-weekly. Transplant nephrectomy was performed in November 2011 and chronic dialysis reinstituted. In February 2012, fever, splenomegaly, anemia (Hb = 8.6g/dL) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count = 50,000/mm3) were observed with 12,870 Leishmania/ml and 60,440 Leishmania/ml of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Thereafter, meglumine antimoniate adapted to renal clearance was administered daily for 28 days, then 1-3 times/week for maintenance. Liver function remained normal. ECG showed a T-wave inversion but troponin remained normal. Fever and sweats resolved, spleen size decreased from 21 to 17 cm, and blood counts normalized in 4 weeks, number of CD4 lymphocytes = 833/mm3 in June 2012,. Leishmania blood PCR and cultures became negative within a month and remained negative over eight monthly evaluations until death in January 2013 due to hypovolemic shock following a dental extraction.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old male three-time renal transplant recipient presented with recurrent febrile visceral leishmaniasis relapses between 2009 and 2012 accompanied by splenomegaly, sweats, and pancytopenia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Initially diagnosed with visceral leishmaniasis by blood PCR in 2004 and cured clinically with liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB), the patient suffered five sequential relapses between August 2009 and February 2012 following intensive anti-rejection therapy (anti-thymocyte globulin, plasmapheresis, rituximab, and steroid boluses) after his third kidney transplant in 2008, persisting despite repeated high-dose L-AmB inductions, maintenance L-AmB infusions (up to twice weekly), a 4-month course of miltefosine, and transplant nephrectomy in November 2011.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage renal disease status post three renal transplants (1979, 1981, and 2008, with graft nephrectomy and return to hemodialysis in November 2011); history of chronic hepatitis B, legionellosis, chronic Q fever, and CMV infection.
subjective.review_of_systems: Prior immunosuppressive regimen included mycophenolate mofetil 1 g/day, tacrolimus 4.5 mg/day, and prednisone 10 mg/day; positive for recurrent fever, sweats, and splenomegaly.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile with sweats and massive splenomegaly (21 cm, decreasing to 17 cm after antimonial therapy).
objective.routine_investigations: During relapses, labs showed anemia (Hb 8.6-9.1 g/dL), leukopenia (WBC 1,200-1,600/mm3), thrombocytopenia (platelets 50,000/mm3), and normal liver function tests. During meglumine antimoniate therapy, ECG showed T-wave inversion with normal serum troponin.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ lymphocyte counts were depressed during relapses (87-186/mm3, recovering to 833/mm3 in June 2012). Quantitative PCR and blood/BAL analyses documented recurrent Leishmania parasitemia (431/mL in Aug 2009; 29.6/mL in Jan 2010; 29.8/mL with positive venous blood Leishmania culture in Jul 2010; 40/mL in Apr-Jun 2011; and 12,870/mL in blood plus 60,440 Leishmania/mL in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in Feb 2012).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Quantitative blood PCR, venous blood culture, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid qPCR confirmed multi-relapsing Visceral Leishmaniasis with pulmonary involvement in a profoundly immunosuppressed renal transplant recipient refractory to liposomal amphotericin B and miltefosine. Following transplant nephrectomy and initiation of renal-clearance-adjusted meglumine antimoniate (daily for 28 days, then 1-3 times weekly maintenance) in February 2012, fever and sweats resolved, blood counts normalized within 4 weeks, CD4 count rose to 833/mm3, and blood Leishmania PCR and cultures remained negative for 8 consecutive months until the patient died in January 2013 from hypovolemic shock following a dental extraction.
